That'll only happen if you're a Linux Newb and you jumped feet first into the world of Gentoo/Arch/Linux from Scratch.

Get someone an install of Ubuntu or one of its derivatives, and they'll be up and running in no time. When they do encounter an issue, help is only a wiki page or a forum post away.

Point is, Linux is "harder" because the user has more choice. They are trusted with control over their system, a concept which Apple and Microsoft crap themselves just thinking about.

I personally disagree with all but those distros and raw Linux being easy to use (as I feel that is what you were saying). I say this having an Arch install on my desktop and Arch on my personal media server.

Between PulseAudio and Wireless drivers, two very important and basically essential "for the average user" things, I've had a hell of a time getting Ubuntu to function as a normal user's machine at times.

I really am sad such a basic thing like sound can be such a bear to deal with.

There have been times it has "just worked", but I'd say it's 50/50 for me so far and I've installed Ubuntu on at least 10+ different systems with varying specs and platforms.

I imagine I'm probably the minority. Admittedly, Windows has been just as spotty for me. Some systems are just problems for some reason, even if troubleshooting doesn't point to hardware.

You are right regarding why Linux is "harder" of course. Just giving my two cents.
